france24fr.title: Arrivée d'El Niño : sommes-nous condamnés à subir ?
france24fr.description: Les spécialistes lui prédisent déjà une puissance colossale. Le phénomène climatique El Niño, qui est censé se déclencher cet été, est de plus en plus redouté. observador.description: O atual presidente da distrital anunciou que volta a candidatar-se "com o compromisso de reforçar a organização interna, valorizar os militantes e apoiar os eleitos locais".

observador.title: Renamo exige posição da África do Sul sobre xenofobia
observador.description: Se até 12 de junho não cessarem os ataques contra nacionais, a Renamo defende que se ocupem empreendimentos dos sul-africanos no país.

observador.title: Depois ficam chocados quando a polícia lhes bate à porta
observador.description: As lideranças de PS e PSD mostram sempre supresa quando as autoridades entram nas juntas de freguesia de Lisboa. Dá vontade de citar a frase famosa: “Você sabe que eu sei que você sabe que eu sei”.

observador.title: Os assassinos de Henry Nowak merecem o nosso rancor
observador.description: O sr. Starmer, primeiro-ministro britânico, não se ajoelhou por Henry Nowak. Aliás, limitou-se a seguir o exemplo dos “media” quase em peso e dedicou ao tema um rigoroso silêncio.

observador.title: Como o historiador Nafafé nos conta a História
observador.description: Os raciocínios de analogia de José Lingna Nafafé são falsos ou estão assentes na teia de erros e confusões que este historiador vem ultimamente espalhando pelos jornais e televisões do nosso país.

observador.title: Mação abre época balnear a 13 de junho após recuperar danos
observador.description: Presidente da câmara indica que os trabalhos de recuperação dos estragos provocados pela tempestade Kristin decorrem "de forma intensa" para garantir o arranque da época balnear em plenas condições.

observador.title: Um morto em incêndio em empresa de construção em Cascais
observador.description: Incêndio, que atingiu um barracão da empresa, ficou dominado pelas 23h40. Foi encontrada uma vítima carbonizada, segundo fonte do Comando Sub-regional da Grande Lisboa.

observador.title: O Cónego Jeremias e o padre que saiu do armário…
observador.description: Nunca pensei que usar a batina diariamente me faria tão feliz como padre. Possibilitou que eu fizesse, na rua, tanto bem que eu não podia imaginar.

observador.title: Associação TáxisRAM contra introdução de 'robotáxis'
observador.description: A associação afirma que não aceita que "decisões tomadas a pensar nas grandes áreas metropolitanas sejam impostas às regiões autónomas sem uma avaliação séria dos impactos económicos e sociais".

observador.title: Plano Nocional de Leitura (XLVII)
observador.description: A tese principal da arte poética de Álvaro de Campos é a de que nenhuma pessoa sensata deve considerar investir em acções ou obrigações poéticas.

observador.title: Parque timorense designado reserva mundial da biosfera
observador.description: A reserva Nino Konis Santana alberga a maior floresta primária remanescente do país, com recifes de coral com cerca de 500 espécies de peixes. Inclui também o Lago Iralalaro.

observador.title: A Europa fluída, os populistas e os "prostitutos"
observador.description: A polémica ficou presa à expressão. O essencial estava noutro lado: na crítica de Passos Coelho ao nacionalismo populista, à política sem convicções e à tentação de combater o populismo imitando-o.

spiegel.title: Keime im Flugzeug: Wie Sie sich an Bord vor Bakterien und Viren schützen
spiegel.description: Am Gurt, auf dem Tisch und der Toilette: Im Flugzeug sind Keime überall. Wie hoch das Risiko einer Infektion wirklich ist und was für Desinfektionsmittel im Handgepäck spricht.

spiegel.title: Camping: Elf Tipps, mit denen Sie richtig Geld sparen
spiegel.description: Ein Wohnmobil als günstige Urlaubsalternative, das war mal. Hier sind die elf besten Hacks vom Campingexperten, mit denen Sie günstiger wegkommen.

spiegel.title: US-Armee attackiert Ziele in Iran – Luftalarm in zwei Golfstaaten
spiegel.description: Das US-Militär berichtet von Drohnenbeschuss aus Iran und greift daraufhin Radarstationen an. Stunden später soll Teheran sieben ballistische Raketen auf Kuwait und Bahrain abgefeuert haben.

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Fifa erlaubt Fans doch Wasserflaschen in den Stadien
spiegel.description: Bei der Fußball-WM in den USA, Mexiko und Kanada drohen Extremtemperaturen. Dass die Fifa Fans trotzdem das Mitbringen von Wasser verbieten wollte, sorgte für Empörung – und eine schnelle Korrektur.

spiegel.title: SpaceX: Kurz vor Börsengang – Mega-Deal mit Google über KI-Rechenleistung
spiegel.description: Google ordert für monatlich 920 Millionen Dollar KI-Rechenleistung bei SpaceX. Der Vertrag läuft bis 2029. Die Details stammen aus Börsenunterlagen und passen Elon Musk gerade bestens ins Konzept.

spiegel.title: EU-Kommission fordert erneut Ende der Grenzkontrollen in Deutschland
spiegel.description: Deutschland und acht weitere Schengenländer kontrollieren derzeit ihre Binnengrenzen. Die EU-Kommission hält das für nicht mehr nötig. Innenminister Alexander Dobrindt widerspricht.

spiegel.title: Ukraine: Kiew entschuldigt sich für sprengstoffbeladene Seedrohne vor Ferieninsel
spiegel.description: Eine vor einer Ferieninsel gefundene sprengstoffbeladene ukrainische Seedrohne sorgt für Wirbel. Der Vorfall wirft Fragen über ukrainische Militäroperationen im Mittelmeer auf.

spiegel.title: Lennart Karl fällt für Fußball-WM aus
spiegel.description: Der 18-Jährige sollte bei der Weltmeisterschaft das deutsche Spiel mitprägen. Nun verpasst er das Turnier wegen einer Verletzung. Der Bundestrainer spricht von einem »Schock« – und nominiert umgehend einen Nachrücker.

spiegel.title: Henry Nowak: Großbritannien wirft USA Einmischung vor
spiegel.description: Die Tötung des Studenten Henry Nowak durch einen Sikh hat in Großbritannien eine hitzige Debatte ausgelöst. Nun hat sich auch US-Vizepräsident JD Vance dazugeäußert. Keir Starmer setzt sich dagegen zur Wehr.

spiegel.title: DFB-Frauen: Deutschland schlägt Norwegen – Qualifikation für WM 2027 in Brasilien geglückt
spiegel.description: Norwegen war ein Härtetest – die DFB-Elf bestand ihn mit Bravour: Trotz improvisierter Abwehr qualifiziert das deutsche Team sich vorzeitig für die WM 2027. Debütantin Marie Müller feierte eine perfekte Premiere.

spiegel.title: Keir Starmer hält russischen Angriff auf Nato in vier Jahren für möglich
spiegel.description: Großbritanniens Premierminister Keir Starmer hat vor einem russischen Angriff auf die Nato in der Zukunft gewarnt. Das Land will deshalb stärker in Verteidigung investieren.

spiegel.title: Tom Schilling hält sein jugendliches Aussehen auch für einen Fluch
spiegel.description: Als Tom Schilling mit »Crazy« seinen Durchbruch feierte, kaufte ihm niemand ab, dass er 18 war. Nun hat er in einem Interview erzählt, wie ihn das als Schauspieler bis heute prägt.

spiegel.title: USA: Gericht erklärt Stopp von Einwanderungsanträgen für rechtswidrig
spiegel.description: Nach Schüssen auf zwei Nationalgardisten verschärft Präsident Trump die Einwanderungspolitik der USA. Unter anderem dürfen keine Greencards und Asylgesuche mehr bewilligt werden. Zu Unrecht, hat nun ein Richter geurteilt.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump plant offenbar Entlassungswelle bei US-Geheimdiensten
spiegel.description: Die Behörden des US-Geheimdienstes werden kleiner: Noch vor Amtsantritt des neuen Koordinators Bill Pulte hat Trump ihn einem Bericht zufolge angewiesen, eine große Zahl von Mitarbeitern zu entlassen.

spiegel.title: Wladimir Putin und Ex-Kanzler Gerhard Schröder führen Vieraugengespräch
spiegel.description: Gerhard Schröder und der russische Präsident Wladimir Putin sollen sich getroffen haben. Putin hatte den Ex-Kanzler zuvor als Vermittler im Ukrainekrieg vorgeschlagen.

spiegel.title: Leck an der Internationalen Raumstation ISS: Die Grenze zwischen Leben und Tod ist etwa so dick wie ein Geldstück
spiegel.description: Die ISS verliert ständig Luft. Nun hatte sich die Situation so zugespitzt, dass ein Teil der Crew in die Rettungskapsel beordert wurde. Das Problem betrifft eines der ältesten Module – und die Mülleimer der Astronauten.

spiegel.title: Mount Everest: Dawa Sherpa stürzte in Gletscherspalte, wurde von Lawine gerettet
spiegel.description: Ein Sherpa verliert Anschluss an seine Gruppe, kriecht Tage später zum Basecamp. Helfer berichten nun, was passiert sein soll: Demnach stieg er allein ab und fiel in eine Gletscherspalte. Eine Lawine rettete ihm das Leben.

spiegel.title: Angriff auf Frau: Hamburger Wolf ist laut Umweltbehörde wahrscheinlich tot
spiegel.description: Der Wolf, der vor gut zwei Monaten eine Frau in der Hamburger Innenstadt verletzt hat, ist vermutlich tot. Der Sender an dem freigelassenen Tier schickt offenbar keine Signale mehr.

elpais.title: León XIV, el pacificador
elpais.description: Robert Prevost ha pasado de ser un misterio, alguien aparentemente pusilánime, a convertirse en dos meses en una revelación. Hombre sosegado cuya mayor preocupación es superar las divisiones, se ha erigido en sorprendente antagonista de Trump y ha arremetido contra el tecnofascismo de Silicon Valley. ¿Qué es lo que piensa este papa y por qué ha resultado tan desconcertante?

elpais.title: El Papa llega a España con un mensaje contra la polarización y el odio al inmigrante
elpais.description: La primera visita de un pontífice en 15 años tiene una fuerte carga política, con un histórico discurso en el Congreso, y es un test decisivo para verificar su línea en el escándalo de la pederastia

elpais.title: León XIV, el visitante más incómodo e inoportuno para Vox
elpais.description: Abascal acudirá al discurso en el Congreso de un Papa a quien su entorno ha calificado de vengativo e idólatra

elpais.description: Estrellas como Puskas, Pelé, Iniesta o Messi han forjado la leyenda dorada del torneo más deseado

elpais.description: La Federación de Asociaciones de Padres y Madres del Alumnado, la Asociación de Directores de Institutos Públicos de Madrid y profesores denuncian la actitud del consejero Mariano de Paco y piden que se tomen medidas

elpais.title: El queso asturiano en peligro de extinción que solo se vende un día al año (este domingo 7 de junio)
elpais.description: El queso de Urbiés fermenta al ritmo de la luna menguante, solo lo hacen tres mujeres en Asturias y corre riesgo de desaparecer

elpais.title: La respuesta correcta de Benito Antonio
elpais.description: Cuando el cantante puertorriqueño se equivocó con La Casita, la respuesta no consistía en defenderlo sin crítica, sino en aplaudirle cuando escuchó y rectificó

elpais.title: La Casita de Bad Bunny: putiferio viejo en odres nuevos
elpais.description: Para las soldadas del feminismo en Internet, lo personal es político hasta que les tocan el perreo, el bisturí o la mala baba

elpais.title: Vox se hace ya con las competencias sobre los menores migrantes no acompañados en tres comunidades tras las cesiones del PP
elpais.description: Los consejeros de la extrema derecha asumen el poder de decisión sobre los niños y adolescentes extranjeros tras los pactos con el PP en Extremadura, Aragón y Castilla y León. Ya han adoptado las primeras medidas

elpais.description: Los chatbots de IA creados por OpenAI y Anthropic son una partida nueva en los contratos de las administraciones

elpais.title: Hostias a domicilio: una ‘telemisa’ para combatir la soledad no deseada
elpais.description: Las parroquias de barrio organizan ceremonias en casas particulares para personas mayores y de movilidad reducida

elpais.title: Negociación a lo “reality show”: los profesores valencianos llegan al vigésimo día de huelga sin acuerdo
elpais.description: Las concentraciones y protestas en apoyo a los docentes se suceden, como el llamamiento de la confederación de madres y padres Gonzalo Anaya a vaciar las aulas

republika.description: Il russo da San Pietroburgo risponde alla lettera dell’ucraino: “Non c’è ragione di un vertice”. Poi vede l’ex cancelliere già bocciato come mediatore dalla Ue. Dagli Stati Uniti 8 miliardi di aiuti a Kiev

republika.description: L’esperto: “Il Cremlino è stato umiliato: ora i falchi potrebbero pressare per dare segnali di un attacco nucleare”

republika.description: C’è l’intesa tra Stato ebraico e Libano, ma la milizia sciita pone nuove condizioni. I vertici di Beirut avvertono: “Teheran smetta di usarci come merce di scambio”

republika.title: Gli ordini di evacuare, poi le bombe: a Tiro restano soltanto le macerie
republika.description: Il quartiere cristiano nella città a sud del Libano, unico risparmiato dall’aviazione, è diventato il rifugio per migliaia di sfollati. Ma l’Idf minaccia: “Cacciate i combattenti sciiti, o colpiremo anche lì”

republika.title: La solitudine di Israele in guerra totale
Giustizia, Forza Italia pretende nuove riforme
republika.description: Il sottosegretario Sisto: “Seguiamo il programma, la prescrizione torni com’era prima”. Ma FdI frena. Prossima settimana nuovo vertice di maggioranza

republika.title: Nordio: “Sanzioni sulla carriera per i magistrati che sbagliano. No alla responsabilità civile”
republika.description: Il ministro della Giustizia: “Il caso Minetti spero serva di lezione a una opposizione che si è scatenata chiedendo le mie dimissioni”

republika.title: Lite sulla legge elettorale: il Pd valuta l’Aventino o il blitz sulle preferenze
republika.description: Giovedì la call tra i leader di opposizione per studiare la strategia: “Niente larghe intese se ci sarà un pareggio nelle urne”

republika.description: L’accusa di essere coinvolto mi ha ferito. E se un mio amico avesse molestato mia sorella, penso che lei melo avrebbe detto

republika.description: La festa per le nozze della diva pop con Callum Turner prende il la in una città blindata. E ora cresce il malumore

nyt.title: Xavier Becerra Advances in California Governor Race
nyt.description: Mr. Becerra was long dismissed in the contest until the abrupt departure of Eric Swalwell created a surprise path for an experienced Democrat.

nyt.title: What to Know About California’s Top Election Races
nyt.description: Spencer Pratt, a Republican running for the role, showed early strength, but Nithya Raman, a progressive city councilwoman, made a substantial leap in Friday’s returns.

nyt.description: Also, job growth is looking healthier. Here’s the latest at the end of Friday.

nyt.title: Graham Platner Controversy Deepens Democratic Unease Before Maine Senate Primary
nyt.description: The party’s politicians, officials and strategists wrestled with how to respond to new reporting about Graham Platner, with worries rising about his vulnerabilities in a general election.

nyt.title: Amid Graham Platner Controversy, Where Does the Maine Senate Race Go Next?
nyt.description: New revelations about Graham Platner have left Democrats anxious.

nyt.description: The latest violence between the United States and Iran threatened a cease-fire and risked further stoking tensions in the region.

nyt.title: Iran’s Soccer Team Allowed Into U.S. for World Cup, but Many Staff Denied
nyt.description: After months of doubts over their participation, Iran’s players have received visas for the United States just days before the World Cup begins.

nyt.title: Stocks Slide as Investors See Rates Rising After Strong Jobs Data
nyt.description: The S&P 500 fell more than 2.6 percent on Friday, its worst one-day drop of the year and ending nine weeks of gains.

nyt.description: Tech titans and Silicon Valley transplants changed the Columbus area, but not everyone is thrilled about the rapid transformation.

nyt.title: U.S. Job Market Pushes Past Shocks and Strains
nyt.description: Employers added 172,000 jobs in May, adding to a vigorous pace of hiring in recent months. But wage growth is not keeping up with higher prices and consumers remain pessimistic.

nyt.title: Why the SpaceX IPO Will Affect Your 401(k), Like It or Not
nyt.description: Elon Musk’s rocket company, on the cusp of the largest initial public offering ever, will soon end up in index funds after rule changes by Nasdaq and other index providers.

nyt.title: Trump Greets Farmers in Wisconsin, but Says He Could Be Home Watching TV
nyt.description: President Trump was in Wisconsin to reassure farmers who have been stung by his tariff policies and rising fuel prices from the war in Iran.

nyt.title: Trump Administration Investigating Gender Treatments at Mount Sinai
nyt.description: A grand jury subpoenaed the health system for information about adolescent patients who had received gender-related care, Mount Sinai said on Friday.

nyt.title: Pentagon Cuts 180 Religious Identities From Military Personnel Records
nyt.description: The new policy, which the Pentagon framed as a largely administrative action, leaves just 31 religious categories to choose from, 22 of which are Christian.

nyt.title: Man Who Schemed With Au Pair to Kill His Wife Is Sentenced to Life
nyt.description: Brendan Banfield was found guilty of murdering his wife and another man, who was lured in through a fetish website. The plan involved his lover, who is now serving 10 years in prison.

nyt.title: First U.S. Screwworm Case Since 1960s Prompts Texas Emergency Response
nyt.description: The infections are the first detected in the United States since the 1960s. Officials are aggressively trying to prevent the parasite from spreading in the nation’s largest cattle-producing state.

nyt.title: ’60 Minutes’ Stars Will Stay After Pelley’s Firing Because They Don’t Want Show to ‘Die’
nyt.description: Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker and Jon Wertheim said on Friday in an email to the show’s staff that they had reached the decision after a period of “grieving” and frustration.

npr.description: At "Russian Davos," Putin ruled out meeting with Zelenskyy and promoted a new world economic order.

npr.title: Xi Jinping will travel to North Korea next week in first visit since 2019
npr.description: The announcement was made by both countries Friday a day after North Korea unveiled a new facility to produce nuclear fuel.

npr.title: South Africa rolls out game-changing HIV shot amid funding shortfalls
npr.description: A new twice-yearly HIV prevention injection could transform South Africa's fight against the epidemic — but U.S. aid cuts and limited doses threaten to slow its impact.

npr.title: China's highest bridge brings tourists and internet access to remote communities
npr.description: A link to the highway that cuts travel times from hours to just minutes, and a symbol of a flow of investment that has provided unprecedented access to high-speed internet in this remote region.

npr.title: Protesters in Albania oppose plan for Trump family-linked resort
npr.description: Protesters in Albania oppose Jared Kushner's planned Adriatic coast resort, which would be located in one of the Mediterranean's most environmentally sensitive areas.

npr.title: Putin says Russia will bolster air defenses in response to Ukrainian drone attacks

npr.title: North Korea unveils a new plant to produce fuel for nuclear weapons

npr.description: The U.N. peacekeeping mission for Lebanon, known as UNIFIL, said one peacekeeper was killed and others were wounded when they came under mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon.

npr.title: Russia's economic forum opens against backdrop of Ukrainian strikes
npr.description: The St. Petersburg International Economic Forum -- Russia's answer to Davos -- opens under the shadow of Ukrainian drone attacks and growing economic uncertainty.

npr.title: Peru election could add to string of right-wing victories in Latin America
npr.description: Peruvians go to the polls Sunday to elect their next president amid a conservative shift in Latin America. The daughter of a former dictator, a far-right senator, could win.

japantimes.title: Japan and Indonesia to begin talks on exporting Asagiri-class destroyers
japantimes.description: The agreement to begin working-level discussions is the latest in a push by Tokyo to transfer defense equipment to like-minded partners.

japantimes.title: Trump’s latest tariff salvo no fix for global issue of forced labor

japantimes.title: In Japan, a bull market for bear deterrents

japantimes.title: At 1 Hotel Tokyo, luxury is a zero-waste journey
japantimes.description: Open from March, the brand's first outpost in Japan stays true to its sustainable roots.

register.description: The plea for caution comes the same week it beat AI archrival OpenAI to filing for an IPO

phys-org.title: Americans share the same struggles despite deep political divides, new bipartisan report finds
phys-org.description: As the United States approaches its 250th anniversary amid deep political division, a major new bipartisan report aims to get consensus on a fundamental question: How are we really doing as a country? The new "State of the States" report, released by the State of the Nation Project at Tulane University, has analyzed more than three decades of data for all 50 states and the District of Columbia, to provide a long-term progress report for each state.

phys-org.title: Scientists map more than 200 years of nature's progress
phys-org.description: Armed with trail cameras, artificial intelligence, and a powerful national research network, scientists are revisiting Lewis and Clark's legendary journey to see how America's wildlife has changed over the past 200 years.

phys-org.title: A new strategy for assembling π-conjugated panels into square molecules revealed
phys-org.description: A research group has developed a new method for selectively synthesizing three-dimensional macrocycles,⁽¹⁾ in which four panels are arranged in a square, by connecting planar π-conjugated molecules⁽²⁾ at right angles.

phys-org.title: Starting kindergarten soon? Summer is a perfect time to support a child's early literacy learning
phys-org.description: The first day of kindergarten is a momentous occasion for children and families. It's an exciting milestone that comes with new friends, teachers, and learning opportunities. It can also bring parental anxiety about whether their child is ready, especially when it comes to early literacy.

phys-org.title: Why do rival plants coexist? The secret is in the soil beneath the oaks
phys-org.description: How can plants that compete for the same resources grow in the same area without one driving the other to extinction? Ecologists have been trying to answer this question for decades, and a surprising new explanation has now emerged: the soil surrounding oak trees acts as a silent mediator that restrains the dominant species and gives an advantage to weaker ones, allowing both to coexist.

phys-org.title: Transnational history explores the Japanese migration to Canada 1877–1988
phys-org.description: "Japanese Migration to Canada, 1877–1988," a new reference essay by Masumi Izumi, was published in the Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Migration Studies. The article offers a sweeping, deeply researched account of Japanese migration to Canada from the arrival of the first documented migrant in 1877 through the Canadian government's formal redress settlement of 1988.

phys-org.title: Physicists discover attractive forces between molecular condensates may cause running off
phys-org.description: Inside cells, certain functions are carried out by locally adjusting molecular composition. This condensation of material results in the formation of dense droplets that can dynamically rearrange. Because of this, interactions between such dense regions determine the shaping of condensates. Scientists from the Department of Living Matter Physics at MPI-DS recently developed a model that can describe such phase separation dynamics based solely on attraction. The work is published in the journal P

phys-org.title: Did this star eat its planets? A new study offers clues on 'chemical paradox' of a binary system
phys-org.description: Astronomers have investigated a puzzling binary star system in which two stars that may have formed together now show dramatically different chemical compositions. The new study, uploaded to the arXiv preprint server on May 29, hints at the possibility that one of the stars may have swallowed its own planets.

phys-org.title: Light pulses uncover Higgs mode that reshapes perovskite crystal symmetry
phys-org.description: Waves of light and sound interact to drive electronic and structural changes in a perovskite crystal. At the atomic scale, nothing is ever truly still. Materials that appear perfectly rigid and motionless to the naked eye are in fact swarms of vibrating atoms. This motion is generally random and uncoordinated, but with the right input, the atoms in certain materials will start to move together, vibrating in sync.

phys-org.title: Hagfish fossils reveal stepwise eye simplification before near-total vision loss
phys-org.description: Many animals, including humans, rely on their eyes to detect changes in their surroundings. The eyes of vertebrates, animals with a backbone or a similar supporting structure, contain a transparent structure (i.e., the lens) that focuses incoming light onto a layer of light-sensitive cells, known as the retina. Cells in the retina then convert light into signals that are sent to the brain.

phys-org.title: Dengue is no longer just a travel risk—what Google's mosquito plan could mean for your summer
phys-org.description: This is not science fiction or some perverse prank. A Silicon Valley tech giant is seeking federal approval to release up to 64 million sterilized male mosquitoes in California and Florida over the next two years.

phys-org.title: Critical Te-104 decay measurements may help answer century-old alpha particle formation question
phys-org.description: University of Tennessee, Knoxville physicists and their colleagues have made critical measurements of the lifetime and decay energy of tellurium-104 (Te-104), an important step in answering a century-old question and understanding how hundreds of nuclei decay. The results are published in Nature.

phys-org.title: First steps: America's grueling second spacewalk
phys-org.description: One year after Gemini IV astronaut Edward H. White completed NASA's first spacewalk the agency prepared for a demanding second excursion. Originally scheduled for Gemini VIII, the extravehicular activity (EVA) was reassigned to Gemini IX-A after that mission ended early, with Gene Cernan taking on the task.

phys-org.title: Europe's aversion to eating insects may have deep ecological and evolutionary roots
phys-org.description: In recent years, human population growth, coupled with the climate crisis, environmental pressures, and current production and consumption patterns, has driven the search for alternative food sources. With 1,611 insect species listed as edible, organizations such as the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) have proposed insects as a sustainable food source.

phys-org.title: Leak on space station triggers brief safety alert
phys-org.description: Astronauts working on the International Space Station briefly sheltered in a docked capsule Friday as Russian colleagues assessed leak repairs, NASA said.

phys-org.title: RNA-guided transposon mechanics show use of figure-eight intermediate and direct-transfer route
phys-org.description: IS110 transposons are a large, diverse family of bacterial insertion sequences (IS elements)—small, mobile DNA elements that can move from one genomic location to another. They have recently attracted broad interest due to the finding that some of these transposons use a bridge RNA (bRNA) to recognize both donor DNA and target DNA.

phys-org.title: Passive AI use at work increases feelings of work meaninglessness, study finds
phys-org.description: Approximately 88% of organizations around the world implemented artificial intelligence (AI) into at least one business function by the end of 2025, the latest McKinsey Global Survey on the state of AI found. Despite promised productivity gains, passive AI use at work, where employees copy-and-paste AI responses to complete tasks, can make people doubt their skills and find their work meaningless, according to a study co-authored by a faculty member from Penn State's Smeal College of Busine

phys-org.title: Geopolitics playing increasing role in investment decisions
phys-org.description: Geopolitical tensions are increasingly influencing where companies choose to invest, according to new research co-authored by a King's academic that suggests firms are becoming more likely to favor politically-aligned countries when making foreign investments.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
proj-syn.description: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.

proj-syn.title: When Markets Run on Empty
proj-syn.description: Markets are flying high despite geopolitical turmoil because a broad-based willingness to keep spending has been matched by an ability to keep doing so. But as more economic participants exhaust their means and rely on debt, a painful moment of truth will arrive—sooner rather than later if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

proj-syn.title: The Pope and the AI Profiteers
proj-syn.description: In his first encyclical, Pope Leo XIV rightly rejects the idea that markets alone can be trusted to shape society’s technological future. Recognizing that AI raises questions that prices and profits cannot answer, the Chicago-born pope has posed a direct challenge to Chicago School economics.

proj-syn.title: AI Must Not Encroach on Human Dignity
proj-syn.description: In a world captivated by technological advances, Pope Leo XIV’s first encyclical seeks to shift attention away from the marvels and terrors of AI and toward the magnificence of humanity. The message that the technology lacks a “moral conscience” and is distinct from human cognition is necessary and welcome.

proj-syn.title: The Key Forces Now Shaping Markets and Geopolitics
proj-syn.description: Three major factors are likely to shape economic and geopolitical outcomes over the next several years: politically unconstrained AI development, a shift from the logic of globalization to zero-sum thinking, and heightened international tail risks. Much could go right, or at least as expected—until it doesn’t.

proj-syn.title: The Living Ghosts of Violent Radicalism
proj-syn.description: Following World War II, the most militant student movements emerged in the former Axis powers as a way to cope with previous generations' complicity. But while the Red Army Faction and others were haunted by memories of past crimes, today's young people have mostly forgotten, and a growing number think far-right politics are cool.

proj-syn.title: Using AI to Test Policy Language
proj-syn.description: Policymakers have long understood that language affects economic behavior, but until recently, there were few tools capable of systematically analyzing its effects. AI may now help close that gap, enabling officials to anticipate how framing and timing can move markets and shift public opinion.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Competitiveness Bogeyman
proj-syn.description: Calls for European leaders to protect domestic industry from "unfairly" subsidized Chinese competition have lately grown louder. But while tariffs might offer temporary relief to a few sectors, they cannot restore Europe's technological leadership, industrial dynamism, or export competitiveness.

proj-syn.title: Putting American Science on a MAGA Leash
proj-syn.description: A draft rule from US President Donald Trump’s White House Office of Management and Budget would subject all scientific research funding to the whims of political appointees, further undercutting a pillar of American power. The goal is to foreclose any future that is plural, contestable, and beyond the president’s control.

proj-syn.title: How Measles Came Roaring Back
proj-syn.description: Bangladesh is facing soaring measles cases not because of a single localized failure, but because of years of systemic erosion. Ultimately, maintaining herd immunity against highly contagious viruses requires relentless attention to supply and demand, as well as to the broader social and institutional foundations of public health.

proj-syn.title: Pete Hegseth’s Dangerous Call to Arms in Asia
proj-syn.description: Much like it did in Europe, the Trump administration has called on US allies in the Indo-Pacific to increase military spending to 3.5% of GDP. But a defense buildup on this scale would jeopardize economic growth and regional unity, and could lead Southeast Asian countries to gravitate toward China’s strategic orbit.

proj-syn.title: The Pope’s AI Vision and Its Limits
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV’s encyclical on AI is clear-eyed about the limits of techno-utopianism. But its vision of technology directed toward human flourishing needs to be extended to include the interests of every sentient being, human and nonhuman, biological or—possibly—artificial.

proj-syn.title: The Iran War Is Fueling a Global Debt Shock
proj-syn.description: Once again, a global crisis is disproportionately burdening countries that did not cause it. Across the Global South, the food- and energy-price shock triggered by the conflict in the Middle East has morphed into a debt shock that demands an urgent international response.

proj-syn.title: Democracy vs. Data Centers
proj-syn.description: As tech companies race to build data centers, communities and lawmakers across the United States are pushing back. Industry leaders frame local opposition as a threat to American competitiveness, but China’s experience shows that unchecked expansion carries serious risks of its own.

proj-syn.title: The Right Incentives for Climate Action
proj-syn.description: As the closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues to disrupt global oil and gas flows, countries are increasingly focusing on short-term energy priorities to the detriment of long-term decarbonization goals. In such a context, the difficult task of designing climate policies that realign incentives takes on new importance.

proj-syn.title: The US and India Have Become Regional Rivals
proj-syn.description: While the US views India as a counterweight to China in Asia, it balks at the idea of Indian regional dominance, preferring a pluralistic order. The Trump administration has gone further by pursuing close ties with Pakistan, apparently hoping that the US and India can remain global partners.

proj-syn.title: Digital Sovereignty Is in the Fine Print
proj-syn.description: Despite efforts to build their own digital industries and infrastructure, most countries remain dependent on American tech firms for the provision of core government services. But government officials can tip the balance of bargaining power by attaching certain standardized provisions to public procurement and services contracts.

proj-syn.title: Trump Wants to Privatize His Presidential Records
proj-syn.description: By enacting the Presidential Records Act in response to Richard Nixon’s malfeasance, the US Congress created a process to limit abuse of power and ensure accountability. Like Nixon, Donald Trump seems determined to avoid accountability, which has led his Justice Department to argue—poorly—that the PRA is unconstitutional.
